project_goal: Build a tiny LLM for legal document summarization.
dataset_support_requirements: Need open-source legal-document datasets for summarization, English only, avoid personally identifiable information.
constraints_and_compliance: No private/confidential client data; output should be concise and plain-language.

selected_model.why: Strong, widely adopted small model suitable for summarization SFT/LoRA; 32k context (max_position_embeddings=32768) fits typical legal-doc inputs; good vLLM support and efficient training on 2x A100 80GB within a 2-day budget.

backup_models.why: Very popular and robust instruction model with very long context (131072) for long legal documents; good vLLM ecosystem; slightly larger than 7B but still practical on 2x A100.

selected_open_datasets.why: Open (CC0-1.0), English legislative text summarization; no obvious PII; input lengths (p95 ~4572 tokens, max ~4999 est) fit comfortably within 32k context for SFT.

Convenient packaged legal summarization dataset (BillSum config previewed) with article->summary pairs; lengths (p95 input ~3741 tokens, max ~4776 est) fit within 32k context; useful as an alternate loader/source.

notes: Context-window check: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct has 32768 max_position_embeddings; both selected datasets’ p95/max input lengths (~3.7k–5k tokens est) are well within this, leaving room for instructions and target summaries.

The joelniklaus/legal_case_document_summarization dataset appears to have extremely long inputs (max ~202k tokens est; p95 ~23k), so it would require aggressive chunking or a longer-context model (e.g., Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct) and careful target-field mapping (its preview showed output=dataset_name, not summary).

For compliance/plain-language outputs: add an instruction template during SFT (e.g., 'Summarize in plain English, concise, no legal advice, no names/addresses') and optionally filter any rare PII-like patterns before training.
